body.target_estimand: \(B=B_\pi(u,v)\) on the unknown-order principal real cubic model; the compact probabilistic delivery satisfies \(\{C_3(P):P\in\mathcal P_+\}\subset\mathcal C^\circ\), while no equality is asserted on the unrestricted published class.
body.estimand_functional: \(\operatorname{Rec}(C)=B_\pi(u,v)\) for \(C\in\mathcal C^\circ\); in particular, \(\operatorname{Rec}(C_3(P))=B_\pi(u,v)\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P_+\).

sampling_model.design: Independent observational sampling from one unknown law \(P\in\mathcal P_+\).
sampling_model.units: The observations \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}\) are identically distributed three-vectors.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no assigned treatment; the directed coefficients \(u\) and \(v\) are structural causal effects in the labeled chain.
sampling_model.overlap: The six discrete chain labels are all admissible, and the positive coefficient, loading, scale, and skewness boxes supply uniform algebraic separation.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The confidence set inverts all ten empirical cubic coordinates jointly; it does not estimate or invert their influence covariance.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The causal effect from \(T\) to \(Y\) is reported as not identifiable from the first three cumulants on the fixed unrestricted one-proxy graph.
Theorem 3.6 concerns a fixed graph with unrestricted real coefficients, not the six-order principal sign chart.
Theorem 3.5 identifies the proxy-graph effect using cumulants through the fourth order.
Theorem 2 gives a closed-form one-latent-component loading recovery using covariance and fourth cumulants.
The source-rank theorem uses stacked cumulant orders and generic rank distinctions to recover source direction.
Propositions 2--4 characterize identifiability through the elimination ideal of a modified polynomial parameterization.
Distribution equivalence compares directed structures through equality or generic overlap of their observational model images.
Concentration inequalities yield honest confidence sets and diameter control for ill-posed inverse problems.
Singularity-robust test inversion permits nonlinear moment inference when the moment covariance matrix is singular.

body.tldr: A principal semialgebraic chart of one-global-confounder three-node chains is globally invertible from its third cumulant tensor alone: the unique rank-two slice locates the root, its signed kernel locates the middle node, and two adjugate contractions recover both edges. The positive compact chamber lies inside this chart and supplies uniform denominator margins. On the exact published fixed proxy graph, an analytic full-ideal argument yields the localized relation \(\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}=0\) and generic degree one on \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\ne0\), without claiming an independently executed basis replication or classification of the exceptional divisor. An opposite-chain covariance overlap and honest bounded-moment inversion complete the contrast and inference results; the exceptional real-fiber atlas remains open.

project_justification.gap: The closest proxy-LvLiNGAM result uses fourth-order cumulants for identification and reports nonidentification through order three on the exact fixed one-proxy graph. Existing work does not give the unknown-order principal sign-chart inverse, its positive-chamber uniform margins, or the analytic localized full-ideal consequence for \(\beta\); the exceptional real fibers and alternate charts are also unclassified.
project_justification.niche: The joint three-variable cubic tensor has chain-specific rank and sign geometry that is invisible to bivariate root enumeration and can collapse both label and coefficient ambiguity.
project_justification.fill: The project proves a constant-cost adjugate recovery map on an explicit principal real chart, derives uniform margins on its positive compact subclass, proves an analytic localized full-ideal result for the exact published map, establishes a covariance-only open overlap, and attaches honest finite-sample inversion. The remaining exceptional real-fiber and alternate-chart classification is stated explicitly as unresolved.

body.related_work: Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorems 3.5--3.6, Figure 3, Appendix C.1.1, and the released \(\texttt{NonGaussianIdentifiability.m2}\) file provide the exact fixed one-proxy graph, the fourth-order estimator, and the reported third-order boundary. The localized theorem is an analytic ideal-membership and localization result for that exact parameterized moment map; it does not claim an independently executed replication of the stored basis or extend the unknown-order positive-class inverse to the published unrestricted class. Cai et al. (2023), Theorem 2.3 and equations (3)--(4), motivate closed-form cumulant extraction for a one-latent component but use covariance with a selected higher order. Schkoda, Robeva, and Drton (2024) motivate the rank diagnostic but stack orders three and four for one latent parent. Garcia-Puente, Spielvogel, and Sullivant (2010), Propositions 2--4, supply the full-elimination-ideal criterion used in the analytic argument. Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant (2011) supply the global-versus-generic fiber distinction used to formulate the exceptional atlas. Ghassami et al. (2020) motivate comparison of model images, while Foygel Barber et al. (2022) treat rational covariance recovery for known explicit-latent graphs rather than cross-label overlap. Babii (2020) and Andrews and Guggenberger (2019) inform the confidence-set inversion, but neither treats exact bounded cubic charts with discrete causal-order selection.
body.technical_internal_limitation: No durable receipt records an independently executed normal-form reduction against the released stored basis, so the note makes no such replication claim. Its localized conclusion instead follows analytically from the exact parameterization, polynomial ideal membership, contraction, and localization. The result is confined to \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\ne0\); the exceptional divisor of the fixed published moment map and the complement of the six principal cubic charts remain unclassified. Known zero-skew fibers and removable zero-column failures show why denominator vanishing alone cannot identify the genuine nonidentification locus.
body.honest_scope: The theorem targets concern global recovery on an explicit principal real cubic chart, quantitative uniform margins and finite-sample coverage on the compact positive probabilistic subclass, an analytic localized degree-one result on the exact fixed published moment map, and an explicit covariance-overlap neighborhood. The positive-class identification theorem does not transfer to the published unrestricted class. The localized theorem applies only on \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\ne0\) and does not classify its exceptional divisor. The remaining all-intersection real-fiber and alternate-chart atlas is open. On the fixed order \(1\to2\to3\), the cubic functional returns the same structural \(T\to Y\) coordinate targeted by the published fourth-order functional; this is a compatibility corollary, not a separate root-solving result.
